daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

An MPR verification team is conducting extensive background checks on the two vice-presidential candidates, Sugiono and Amran, following the unprecedented mid-term vacancy. The team visited the Supreme Court to verify bankruptcy status and criminal records, will verify tax and wealth declarations with the Finance Ministry and KPK, and will visit the Defence Ministry to verify the high school diploma of one candidate. The verification process comes after an MPR team member blamed the 2024 presidential election organizers for lacking thoroughness in candidate screening.

  • The MPR team declared the citizenship documents of both vice-presidential candidates Amran and Sugiono valid, and requested verification of citizenship status for the candidates and their wives.
  • Bareskrim identified six social media accounts used to attack the government in the ongoing treason case involving former police chief Listyo Sigit and others.
  • A civilian suspect in the wiretapping case targeting President Prabowo and other officials was identified as a manager at a Bogor regency BUMD and has been immediately dismissed by the regent.
  • In a court hearing on the controversial police law, a witness testified that provisions exempting education requirements were never discussed by Commission II of the DPR during the legislative process.
  • An attorney named Ari Yusuf Amir emphasized that lawyers' income does not come from the police and that professional integrity cannot be negotiated, amid ongoing legal controversies.
  • The requirement for coalition parties to propose two vice-presidential candidates to the MPR has been challenged at the Constitutional Court.
  • An activist group criticized the lack of progress in the case of a fishing crew member's death on the Juanna Bay vessel, insisting the state must not lose against powerful interests.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo's recent state visit to China has yielded US$86.8 billion in trade and investment deals, significantly boosting bilateral economic cooperation. An analyst noted that Prabowo's diplomacy has won praise from three global powers. Meanwhile, Kazakhstan is preparing 20 bilateral agreements ahead of President Prabowo's upcoming visit to the Central Asian nation.

  • Indonesian authorities foiled the recruitment of 21 Indonesian citizens as mercenaries for Russian forces.
  • Indonesia is pushing for an ASEAN Protocol to combat cross-border online scams affecting the region.
  • Tourist arrivals from Kazakhstan to Indonesia reached 26,000 through September, marking an increase in bilateral people-to-people exchanges.
  • The Bandung city government is moving quickly to repatriate the body of a Sukajadi resident from Poland.

Other

Danantara, the new state holding company, is targeting up to Rp6 trillion in profit for 2027, though the company's director Pandu warned that profit could fluctuate by Rp2 trillion depending on rupiah movements. The government's tax incentive programs for 2026 are projected to reach Rp576.4 trillion, according to a minister.

  • The government will open registration for 154,052 civil service positions starting 27 November, including over 30,000 positions for teachers, lecturers, and education staff.
  • The Indonesia Stock Exchange will announce suspected cases of stock manipulation to the public.
  • Indonesia is advancing reviews across 25 policy areas as part of its bid to join the OECD, and will begin implementing APEC investment commitments in 2027.
  • The prosecution received the transfer of three corporate suspects responsible for forest fires in West Kalimantan, while 72 orangutans have been rescued from fires in the province since August.
  • Heti Mulyati was elected as replacement rector of IPB University for the 2023-2028 term, succeeding Alim Setiawan.
